annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Artificial intelligence — The consequences of artificial intelligence on the (digital) single market, production, consumption, employment and society'
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Artificial intelligence — The consequences of artificial intelligence on the (digital) single market, production, consumption, employment and society'
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 288/1
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: 2017 EESC own-initiative opinion on AI's societal consequences. It calls for a human-in-command approach, a global code of ethics, standards for verifying and validating AI, European AI certification, and EU leadership on global frameworks. It opposes legal personality for robots, supports a ban on autonomous weapons, and addresses employment and skills.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for a human-in-command approach where machines remain machines and people keep control.
Calls for a uniform global code of ethics and an EU-led global policy framework for AI.
Opposes any legal personality for robots or AI because of moral hazard and weakened liability law.
Calls for standards for verifying, validating and monitoring AI, plus European AI certification and labels.
Supports a ban on autonomous weapon systems and urges the UN consultation to cover cyber warfare.
